summary: USB root-hub cascade enumeration race stalls SCCM/Intune check-in after laptop dock hot-swap
description: After users hot-swap their laptops onto certain USB-C docks, machines intermittently fail to complete SCCM and Intune check-ins. Agents report stuck 'device-registration' states and the SCCM client shows 'Pending Actions: 0' while heartbeat is missing. The failure window typically occurs within 30s of dock attach and often correlates with multiple USB hubs enumerating simultaneously.
impact: Multiple engineers in US-West cannot receive policies or software during provision/repair. Check-in failure prevents Autopilot/MDM manifest application and delays ticket completions. Estimated ~12 devices affected over the last 48 hours; several are in active repair workflows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Boot laptop (clean image) and do not connect dock. 2) Once logged in, attach USB-C dock (Dell WD22/ThinkPad Thunderbolt 4 dock models observed). 3) Observe Device Manager -> multiple 'USB Root Hub (USB 3.0)' entries appearing rapidly, then one or more devices toggle 'Unknown device' briefly. 4) Run 'ccmexec' and 'dsregcmd /status' to watch check-in. 5) SCCM client stalls on 'Policy request' and Intune MDM agent remains in 'Pending' for >10 minutes. Repro rate ~40% on affected combos.
observed_logs: SCCM client log (locationservice.log): 'Failed to resolve MP. Trying fallback...'; ClientIDManagerStartup.log: 'Register failed - error 0x8024402f'. System event log: 'DriverFrameworks-UserMode (UMDF) Warning: Device did not respond during enumeration'. Kernel logs show bursts of 'usb 1-1: new high-speed USB device number 10' followed by 'usb 1-1: device descriptor read/64, error -71' on some retries.
investigation: Initial triage by Desktop Platform found a race between the dock's internal hub enumeration and the Windows USB host controller driver (xhci). Reproduced on our lab X1 Carbon and a Dell Latitude with WD22. Disabling 'fast startup' reduced but did not eliminate repro. Captured USBPcap traces and compared timestamps: multiple hubs initialize in <200ms window causing host controller queue starvation and a failed device descriptor read (~error -71) that correlates with SCCM client timeouts. No recent SCCM client changes; suspect regression introduced in dock firmware or Windows USB power policy interaction after Feb cumulative update. Cross-referenced INT-241999 for earlier Autopilot-related USB timing regressions.
temporary_workaround: Ask technicians to fully unplug dock, reboot laptop, then attach dock after Windows login and settle for ~60s. Alternative: plug in dock using a different downstream port (some ports showed lower repro). As a faster mitigation, disable selective suspend for USB Root Hub under Power Options in affected devices (manual step).
resolution_plan: 1) Reproduce problem consistently in lab with Windows 11 23H2 + patched cumulative update to capture full traces. 2) Work with Dock vendor to get pre-release firmware and test. 3) Engage Windows platform team to review xHCI timing and host controller queue handling (attach captured USBPcap and ETW traces). 4) If vendor/unix rejects, implement a provisioning script that delays MDM agent startup until 90s after dock attach as a temporary rollout for new images. Target: rollback window or vendor fix within 2 weeks.
